report:
**Conclusion:** The claim is **not supported by high-quality evidence**. Induced abortion has not been shown to increase a woman’s risk of breast cancer.

The National Cancer Institute (NCI) states that its 2003 expert workshop concluded that “induced abortion is not associated with an increase in breast cancer risk.” The American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists likewise says abortion does not increase breast-cancer risk.

Some older case-control studies reported an association, but these studies can be vulnerable to *reporting/recall bias*—women with breast cancer may be more likely to disclose a prior abortion than comparable women without cancer. Larger analyses using prospectively recorded pregnancy data are more reliable for this question. A major collaborative reanalysis of 53 studies (including about 83,000 women with breast cancer) found no increased risk in the prospective-data studies; the relative risk for induced abortion was reported as 0.93, consistent with no increase.

This conclusion concerns breast-cancer risk specifically; individual risk is more strongly influenced by factors such as age, family/genetic history, alcohol use, breast density, and some reproductive/hormonal factors.

Sources:  
- https://www.cancer.gov/types/breast/abortion-miscarriage-risk  
- https://www.acog.org/womens-health/faqs/induced-abortion  
- https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0140673604158352  
- https://www.cancer.org/cancer/risk-prevention/medical-treatments/abortion-and-breast-cancer-risk.html
